C9000251.statement: Adversarially audit, verify, or refute OpenAI Manuscript Family 251 (Amenability, unitarizability, and strong Ulam stability.; papers: Unitarizability implies amenability for discrete groups; Strong Ulam Stability Characterizes Amenability; Lean status: Partially/Comparator formalized (lean/docs/251.md)): either (a) discover and certify an explicit mathematical flaw, sign/orientation error, counterexample to an intermediate lemma, or statement-fidelity/citation gap with a deterministic symbolic/computational certificate (`verify.py` + `exact_certificate.json`), or (b) independently verify, repair, or generalize the manuscript's core mathematical theorem with a standalone machine-checkable certificate certified by the independent Reviewer.

C_SCOPE.statement: Known amenable, free-subgroup, and specified wreath-product results do not settle either general converse; finite-dimensional stability and placeholder comparators are not substitutes.

C_US_MAIN.statement: Strong-Ulam thm:main: a countable discrete group is strongly Ulam stable if and only if amenable.

C_US_AMENABLE.statement: Kazhdan's known amenable direction: every amenable group is strongly Ulam stable, uniformly over all Hilbert spaces, not merely finite dimensions.

C_US_LIST.statement: lem:uniform-list: finite lists simultaneously concentrate at every boundary point and obey the distinguished-point condition.

C_US_FLAGS.statement: prop:flags: nonamenability supplies arbitrarily long finite alphabets and translated flags satisfying F1-F3; repetitions preserve them.

C_US_SPARSE.statement: lem:sparse: two signed orthonormal bases and anticommuting J,Z have uniformly small sparse Gram and J restrictions in sufficiently large dimensions.

C_US_PRIORITY.statement: lem:priority and eq:priority-map: the actual block-Schur isometry and nested comparison have dimension-free O(h) and O(h eta) bounds.

C_US_TRUNCATE.statement: lem:truncate: a near-identity unitary can be changed by at most 3e to fix the designated subspace exactly.

C_US_BUILD.statement: The actual Clifford metrics, arrival frames, endpoint exchanges, and priority projections satisfy positivity, orthogonality, reducing-subspace, and compression hypotheses.

C_US_FRAME.statement: eq:frame-circuit-cost: changing the pair's arrival frames to the triple's costs O(N eta), with no label-count factor.

C_US_CANCEL.statement: eq:common-cancel: F1 makes later added common exchanges commute with earlier surviving exchanges, so a common right factor cancels exactly.

C_US_PROTECTED.statement: eq:post-unitary and eq:next-protected: the actual nested-transfer error acts only at its arrival level and is O(h eta) on the actual next departure.

C_US_SWEEP.statement: eq:moved-errors: truncation and the true adjacent-layer support allow priority errors to be collected on orthogonal levels, costing O(h)+O(N h eta), not O(N h).

C_US_COMPARE.statement: prop:comparison: ||V_qp^{pair}-V_qp^{triple}|| <= C h+C N eta+C N h eta, uniformly in levels, alphabet sizes, and configurations.

C_CC_EXPLICIT.statement: For the actual construction, h <= 1/128 and eta <= 1/4 imply ||V_qp^{pair}-V_qp^{triple}|| <= 40h+16N eta+30N h eta. No disputed estimate is assumed.

C_CC_EXTENSION.statement: The same recipe for arbitrary finite nested configuration sets has bound 40h+16N delta+30N h zeta when the actual sparse Gram and priority-compression errors are delta,zeta <= 1/4.

C_CC_FORMAL_CORE.statement: For every monoid and every finite length, corrected errors commuting with later layers factor out of the interleaved product; in every ring, two-sided annihilating errors commute, disjoint-error products equal identity plus their error sum, and the actual directed-exchange multiplication has arrival error S3^{-1}S2.

C_US_DEFECT.statement: eq:defect-bound: equivariance and three pair-to-triple comparisons bound the normalized map's defect.

C_US_TRANSPORT.statement: lem:transport: all but 2N beta of labels have transport error O(N eta)+O(N h eta).

C_US_WITNESS.statement: lem:witness: the Clifford quadratic form is zero for representation-transported vectors and 1/2 for initial vectors, forcing distance at least 1/4.

C_US_PARAMETERS.statement: The final L,eta,beta order makes defect arbitrarily small while preserving a fixed distance greater than 1/10.

C_FINITE_FLAGS_EXCLUSION.statement: On a finite group, summing F2 and F3 over one stage forces beta >= 1/2. Such models cannot test the actual small-beta construction.

C_U_MAIN.statement: Unitarizability thm:main: a discrete group is amenable iff unitarizable; every nonamenable group has nonunitarizable representations with uniform norm <=1+epsilon.

C_U_AMENABLE.statement: The Day-Dixmier invariant-mean argument unitarizes every uniformly bounded representation of an amenable discrete group.

C_U_CONTRACT.statement: lem:contracting-average: nonamenability gives a finite S containing e and rho<1 with |||S|^{-1} sum R_s|| <=rho.

C_U_SPARSE.statement: prop:sparse-splitting: labelled product lists admit assignments with at most r=ceil(n rho^ell) row ones and column zeros, preserving coincident-product multiplicities.

C_U_FRAMES.statement: lem:frames: k=ceil(2r log(2n)) admits n unit vectors with synthesis norm <=10 on every set of size <=min(2r,n).

C_U_MASKED.statement: lem:masked, cor:block-rows-columns, prop:uniform-differences: labelled-edge factorization gives row/column and conjugation-difference norms <=100.

C_U_ENERGY.statement: eq:kernel-energy and eq:dimension-ratio: positivity gives E >= n even for repeated products, while k/n tends to zero.

C_U_KERNEL.statement: lem:kernel-obstruction: E <=4k(K+||T-C||)^2 for every translation-commuting C under the stated row/column hypotheses.

C_U_DIRECT.statement: prop:direct-sum-obstruction: uniform cocycle bounds and E_j/k_j tending to infinity yield a bounded triangular representation that is not unitarizable.

C_U_INDUCTION.statement: lem:subgroup-induction: induction preserves the uniform bound and the obstruction, extending a countable subgroup witness to a discrete supergroup.

C_U_LOCALITY.statement: The unitarizability manuscript uses the Folner finite-set criterion to put nonamenability in a finitely generated, hence countable, subgroup before induction to an arbitrary discrete group.
